title: Blend sounds into a word
goal: Use a taught spelling pattern to attempt a word, check its pronunciation and connect it with meaning.
cue: Point to m, a and t. Say their word sounds, not their letter names. Join /m/ to /æ/, then finish with /t/: mat. Do not add an extra vowel after t.
spelling: One spelling can represent one sound here. Join the sounds from left to right; then say the whole word naturally.
task: Read mat, sat and map without playing the model first. Then listen and correct one sound.
story: Sam sat. Sam sat on a mat.

articulation.label: mat
articulation.alt: mat: /m/ → /æ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: sat
articulation.alt: sat: /s/ → /æ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: map
articulation.alt: map: /m/ → /æ/ → /p/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: Sam
articulation.alt: Sam: /s/ → /æ/ → /m/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: Angry or annoyed. I am mad because my toy is broken.
be able to do something. I can swim.
put clothes on yourself or someone. He gets dressed before he eats breakfast.
feeling unhappy. He is sad that there are no lessons at the weekend.
feeling pleased. Puck is happy with the class.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.
